slide-003.title: Macro-Environmental Analysis - Social-Social Factors Analysis
body: Analysis of trends and causes:
The resulting inspiration or impact on the company:

Phenomenon/Trend 1: Population Growth and Migration in North America
Population Growth: The U.S. population was approximately 340.4 million in 2024, representing a 1% annual increase (net immigration accounted for over 70% of the growth); Canada's population was approximately 41.3 million, representing a 1.8% annual increase;
Policy Disturbance: Since 2025, the U.S. has tightened immigration policies, leading to a slowdown in net immigration inflow. Institutions forecast that population growth may decline to 0.3%-0.5% in 2025-2026, with a tightening supply of skilled construction technicians;
Population Migration: Texas, Florida, North Carolina, Georgia, South Carolina, and Tennessee experienced rapid population growth, with growth rates exceeding 1.1%.
Phenomenon/Trend 2: Consumer Behavior and Demand
Demand for Efficient and Reliable Equipment: According to survey results, U.S. customers are less price-sensitive and tend to prefer overall reliable and efficient machinery.
Phenomenon/Trend 3: Persistent Shortage of Skilled Labor in Construction
According to a survey by the Associated General Contractors of America (AGC), over 70% of contractors reported difficulty in hiring, with labor shortages becoming a bottleneck for project schedules. Customers' willingness to purchase automated functions such as assisted driving and remote control has significantly increased;
Phenomenon/Trend 4: Media Consumption Structure
Pervasiveness of Digital Media: YouTube has become the primary video content platform, with over 2 billion monthly active users, featuring extensive product operation training, feature promotion, and user reviews. Other digital platforms such as Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok, which focuses on short videos, are also growing rapidly. The share of short videos and AI-generated content in equipment marketing has further increased.
Decline in Influence of Traditional Media: With digital transformation, the influence of traditional media such as newspapers and television has gradually weakened, although they still maintain a certain market share among specific audiences, particularly in local news and industry-specific reporting.
Professional Forums and Communities: There are numerous professional construction equipment forums (such as Heavy Equipment Forums) and professional social platforms like LinkedIn in North America. These platforms have become the primary channels for construction equipment professionals to obtain information and communicate.
1. Increased demand for buildings: This will increase demand for housing and infrastructure, thus contributing to the growth of the excavator market.

2. North America is a highly mature market for engineering machinery, with clients being more selective about products. Product design requires a high degree of attention to product reliability and efficiency, reliable and efficient labelling, as well as a long-range failure diagnostic system for equipment, analysis of equipment performance data and timely identification of potential problems.

3. The construction industry ' s shortage of skilled workers and the continuous rise in claims for automation, with proposals to speed up product packaging and market promotion of smart functions such as assistive driving, remote operation, forecast maintenance as core outlets to respond to customer “job difficulty, cost-benefit” pain points and to increase product premium capacity;

4. Diversity of access to information: Clients and practitioners in the construction equipment industry are increasingly dependent on digital flatnits, such as YouTube, for information on product operations, maintenance and maintenance training, which forces OEM to strengthen content production and brand promotion on these platforms in order to better reach target client groups. In 2025, Caterpillar, John Deere and Sany placed ads on YouTube.
Transforming marketing strategies: Increased investment in digital media is needed, particularly through targeted advertising to raise brand visibility and market penetration. At the same time, emphasis needs to be placed on community interaction and close contact with users through forums, socializations and a sense of loyalty and participation.

slide-007.title: Macro-environmental analysis - Political - Analysis of political factors
body: Analysis of trends and causes:
The resulting inspiration or impact on the company:

Case/trend 1: The tariff structure of China continues to evolve and the combined tax burden remains high
United estimate tariffs on China have been subject to several rounds of adjustment since 2025: the “fentanyl tariff” (10 per cent) and “reciprocal duty” (up to 34 per cent, 24 per cent suspended for one time), based on IEEPA plus a combined increase of about 20 per cent; In February 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that IEEPA tariffs lacked legal authorization and that the United estimate had ceased to collect them as of 24 February, but imposed a 10 per cent temporary surcharge on all trading partners under article 122 of the Trade Act (due to expire on 24 July, which would be supplemented by 301 provisions with similar rates); The current Chinese tariff of 301 (7.5 per cent to 100 per cent) was unaffected and continued to be fully levied, with 178 product exemptions extended until 10 November 2026. China's tariff burden on United estimate exports of engineering machinery has evolved from a “temporary build-up” to a “structural norm”; The current United estimate import tariff of the excavators is 52 per cent, with an increase of 2-10 per cent in August.
Epidemic/trend 2: Continued rise of trade protectionism, increasing demands for “double backs” and localization
The United estimate has initiated or reviewed a “double-reverse” investigation into multiple types of engineering machinery-related products such as engine, chassis and components; (a) The anti-dumping finality (XCMG rate of 24.32 per cent) imposed by the United Kingdom on Chinese crawler excavator in 2025, an anti-absorption review initiated in 2026 and pressures for overseas trade relief continued to grow; Federally funded projects such as IIJA, Buy America, have become more stringent in terms of enforcement, and the “Great and United estimate” bill's full depreciation preference for investment in equipment has increased the relative attractiveness of home-grown production;
Scenario/trend 3: geopolitical and compliance review risks remain prominent
In the United estimate, import regulations for Chinese construction equipment products have been maintained at a constant high level, with stringent requirements such as spot checks, technical certifications and review of TCF documents. Compliance uncertainties in terms of mechanical performance, material composition and environmental indicators remain high.

1. Tariffs have evolved from a phased shock to structural costs, requiring long-term coping mechanisms in the areas of product pricing, equipment classification, amphibious insurance and territorialized capacity deployment, rather than merely short-term evasion.

To follow closely trade relief developments in major overseas markets, such as the United States and the United Kingdom, to assess in advance the impact of related rates on the competitiveness of different tonnages and equipment products; The competitiveness of products continues to be strengthened from the standpoint of controllability, operational efficiency, traderbility and equity.

3. Great importance needs to be attached to the completeness and accuracy of the product TCF documents, which will be reviewed and optimized quickly by the Joint Research General Institute and the Plant Research Institute under the leadership of American Research.

In conjunction with incentives such as the full depreciation of equipment/plant investments under the “Great and Beautiful” Act, an assessment of the feasibility of localizing capacity in the United States and friendly countries and increasing the proportion of territorialized purchases against long-term business risks associated with tariff escalation.

As a result of inflation, interest rates on loans continued to rise, construction costs increased, housing demand declined and the engineering machinery market cooled by heat.

body:
Kubota: Japanese brand, focus on microcompact excavator.
In terms of product performance. Kubota focuses on microcompact excavator products, which have been under cultivation in the North American market share many years and are technologically mature, with microcompact Excavatormarketshare firmly ranked first. XCMG still has significant catch-up space in microcompact excavator hydraulic system calibration, controllability and detailed processes. From the client structure and application landscape. The XCMG target is highly aligned with the client base of the conservation field, concentrated mainly on small and medium-sized clients, typically characterized by operationality and reliability, reliance on finance or leasing, price sensitivity, short procurement path for decision-making, and high impact on oral transmission. Kubota represents the core image of the micro excavator main client group. The Kubota standard helps XCMG to establish product designs, marketing pathways and service logic that are consistent with the value preferences of the target group.
In terms of branding. Kubota is a model for “upgrading from price to value competition”. Kubota, as a representative of “High Value + High Resale Value + High Stability”, provides XCMG with a template for technology, services and overall brand upgrading.

Caterpillar Pyler: the flagship of global engineering machinery, leader of high-end products.

Caterpillarpile is the technical benchmark for Central America's large excavator product, which represents the “gold standard” of North American construction equipment, and a cross-reference to Caterpillar Pill can help XCMG to set standards for the design of midrange excavator for global markets.

Target Cat is a key step in upgrading the XCMG from “price-oriented” to “value-led” brands, and price advantage can only be truly convincing if product strength is close to Caterpillar.
In terms of business policy. Caterpillar’s strong financial system supports finance leasing, resale value buy-back, and flexible payments, which can help XCMG to build its own complete “product+financial+purchase+remanufacturing” programme model and enhance customer stickyness.
In terms of post-market policy, Caterpillar has a well-developed service network in the North American region, with spare parts reaching 24 to 48 hours and providing mature equipment resale value closed service systems. Services and spare parts are key to the success of XCMG in the North American market. Transport scenes - the usual type of transport engine
Standard flatbed trailer

Standard flatbed trailers are a very common type of trailer. While they have several different dimensions (including 24, 40, 45, 48 and 53 feet), 48-foot flatbed trailers are the most commonly used. Multifunctionality is a key feature of these trailers. Usually used for the transport of steel, construction equipment, wood and other open commodities, flat-board vehicles are open on their backs and sides to facilitate handling through forklifts or scooters. The maximum height and width of any cargo transported using these trailers is 8 feet 6 inches (2591 mm), which can be used for the bulk transport of 8 tons of microcompact excavator products. The flat-bed trailer is five feet from the ground, with a maximum load of 48,000 pounds (2177kg). Because it does not have a container to accommodate its contents (such as dry vans), standard flatbed trailers can be used for the transport of super-large cargo, provided the necessary permits are obtained and appropriate routes are followed. Standard flat-bed trailers and all other trailers must be fixed correctly with chain, tape and various tarpaulin solutions.

Transport scenes - the usual type of transport engine
Landing/staircase trailer

When the height of the cargo is a constraint, landing or staircase trailers are often used as alternatives to flat-bed trailers. The simplicity of flat-board vehicles, combined with their increased high capacity, makes land-fall trailers a common mode of transport. The surface trailers, consisting of top decks and rear parts close to the ground level, can drag cargo up to a height of 10 feet and 2 inches (3099 mm) to be considered as exceeding the standard. The flat-board vehicle is usually five feet from the ground, while the landing trailer is much shorter at a minimum of three foot six inches. In the 53-foot pattern, these trailers have 10 and 43-foot lengths on deck and below deck, respectively. Because of its multifunctional nature and ability to carry higher cargoes, staircase trailers are a widely available option among global carriers. You usually see tow trailers carrying agricultural and construction materials, as well as various types of machinery that are suitable for a 10-foot 2-inch limit.
